message.abstract: <jats:p>We give an algebraic characterization of the syntax and semantics of a class of untyped functional programming languages.</jats:p><jats:p>To this end, we introduce a notion of 2-<jats:italic>signature</jats:italic>: such a signature specifies not only the <jats:italic>terms</jats:italic> of a language, but also <jats:italic>reduction rules</jats:italic> on those terms. To any 2-signature (<jats:italic>S, A</jats:italic>) we associate a category of ‘models’. We then prove that this category has an initial object, which integrates the terms freely generated by <jats:italic>S</jats:italic>, and which is equipped with reductions according to the rules given in <jats:italic>A</jats:italic>. We call this initial object the <jats:italic>programming language generated by</jats:italic> (<jats:italic>S, A</jats:italic>). Models of a 2-signature are built from <jats:italic>relative monads</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>modules</jats:italic> over such monads. Through the use of monads, the models – and in particular, the initial model – come equipped with a <jats:italic>substitution operation</jats:italic> that is compatible with reduction in a suitable sense.</jats:p><jats:p>The initiality theorem is formalized in the proof assistant Coq, yielding a machinery which, when fed with a 2-signature, provides the associated programming language with reduction relation and certified substitution.</jats:p>
title: Modules over relative monads for syntax and semantics
